piece_title: F7 — the water surface, round 3. The two RI-VIS04 §9 MIN BAR components the r2 verdict measured as absent: depth-based colour, and a shoreline depth fade.

critic.note: I built none of this. My brief quoted the build's claims up front, which departs from CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8's ordering; recorded rather than hidden. I inherited no figure from the brief, from the status file or from the r2 verdict: every number below was produced this turn by a command I ran or a tool run I launched, and where I quote the build's figure I say it is the build's. Two numbers the brief handed me were WRONG and I say so below (the blind-gate census, and 'shore-close-c is the only one of the three with a real bank in it').

build.the_change: The body colour becomes `mix(esDeepCol, esBedCol, exp(-k*path))` — Beer-Lambert extinction over the water column depth carried in province.js's per-vertex colour, against the region's own `k` from game/data/world/water.json, delivered through a new `uWaterK` uniform resolved at draw time from `object.name`. Plus a shoreline alpha fade `diffuseColor.a = mix(a, a*.42, esTrans*uWaterShoreFade)`, scaled by its own uniform so it can be ablated separately.
build.builders_own_ruling: KEEP as a PARTIAL delivery. Not claiming F7.
build.note_on_candour: This status file damages its own headline three times in its own opening section, and two of the three are correct. The third is not: it reports M12 `NormalEnergy` as 'still not measured, a fourth round running' while its OWN artifact records a number for it at seven of the nine poses it took. A build that is harsh on itself is still a build asserting something it did not check, and this one inherited that assertion from three prior rounds' summaries rather than reading its own JSON.

bifurcation.fidelity: Judged against modern references only: `RI-VIS04` §9's MIN BAR and TELL, `RI-WLD10` §10's fidelity clause, `RI-VIS03` M12. Every number below is on this side.
bifurcation.art_direction: `RI-WLD10` §10.1's art-direction clause — 'water is opaque before it is reflective; every region declares an extinction coefficient k' — is cited once, for the region model, and judged against Morrowind/`RI-WLD05` conventions, not against a modern plate. No modern reference is cited for it.

the_headline: ROUND 3 DELIVERED BOTH MISSING MIN BAR COMPONENTS AND THEY ARE REAL. I confirmed the build's strongest claim under a harder control than it applied, and then found the reason it could not see its own best result: THREE ROUNDS OF F7 HAVE BEEN SHOT IN THE ONE REGION OF THIRTEEN WHERE THE FEATURE CANNOT SHOW. I photographed a second region — the Western Rootlands, k = 1.9 — for the first time in this piece's history. There the shoreline fade takes the waterline transition from **1 px to 15 px**, the depth-colour half moves mean luma **120× the drift floor** where it was inert at k = 4.5, and a **matched-luminance** S52 null reproduces the ENTIRE brightness change while producing **none** of the width. The build's own pessimism about its colour half is therefore wrong, and it is wrong because it never left the Deep Marshes. THE SCORE IS STILL 3: the blind gate has never run, the depth-buffer mechanism the bar's parenthetical names is absent by the builder's own design, M12 two-or-more-fails at a `water_edge` shot in BOTH regions, and at every player pose in the Deep Marshes the fade is 1 px wide on both arms.

job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.the_claim: The k response is monotonic at top-down 120 m — luma 69.066/68.053/65.853/57.608 and gradient width 5/7/13/19 as k goes 4.5/2.6/1.4/0.35 — and S52's null cannot fake it. The brief told me to attack this hardest.
job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.ruling: **IT SURVIVES, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN THE BUILD COULD SHOW. ONE HALF OF THE HEADLINE IS FALSIFIED: WIDTH IS NOT MONOTONIC IN k.**
job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.attack_1_the_mask_is_arm_dependent_and_t: `f7-r3-sweep.mjs` derives a SEPARATE water mask per arm by differencing the frame against a water-hidden frame at |dRGB| > 6. Round 3 is the first F7 round whose change touches ALPHA, so it is the first round where an arm can move its own mask — and `gradient_width_px` is computed from a distance transform OF THAT MASK. If the mask moves, the measure moves for free. THIS IS THE STRONGEST AVAILABLE ATTACK AND THE BUILD DID NOT MAKE IT.
job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.attack_1_result: **THE ORDERING SURVIVES A PINNED MASK AT THREE THRESHOLDS.** I recomputed every top-down arm over ONE mask (the untouched control's), at |dRGB| > 4, 6 and 10. Deep Marshes, pinned, thr 6: prefix 3, fixed 5, no-shorefade 3, null-const-trans 3, k2.6 7, k1.4 14, k0.35 19. At thr 4: 3/5/3/3/7/14/19. At thr 10: 3/5/3/3/9/13/19. The k ordering holds in all three, and the mask confound has the OPPOSITE SIGN to the result — the low-k arms LOSE mask pixels (451,091 vs 455,490), which shortens distance-from-land and would push width DOWN, not up. Tool and output: `artifacts/W1-F7-WATER-r3-critic/reprofile/`.
job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.attack_2_a_properly_matched_s52_null_whi: The build's null pins transmittance at a CONSTANT 0.08 — a value that happens to match the mean transmittance at k = 4.5, which is why it reproduced the luma change there almost exactly. That is a null matched on the proxy, which is the right design. But it has never been run at a k where 0.08 is NOT the right constant, so it has never been shown to fail for the right reason. I ran it at the Western Rootlands at **nullTrans = 0.74**, chosen to match the real arm's luminance.
job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.attack_2_result: **THE CLEANEST S52 RESULT F7 HAS PRODUCED.** Western Rootlands, top-down 120 m, one process, drift floor 0.009% on luma (control 106.602 vs fixed 106.607): prefix luma 113.701 width **1**; fixed 106.607 width **15**; **null-const-trans at t = 0.74 luma 105.251 width 1**. The null OVER-reproduces the entire brightness change (118% of it) and produces **none** of the width. `mean_luma` remains a brightness proxy exactly as S52 says; `gradient_width_px` is not one, and this is now demonstrated at matched luminance rather than argued.
job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.attack_3_is_it_the_colour_half_or_the_al: The build could not decompose the low-k darkening because it never crossed the k arms with the shore-fade arm. I did not run that cross either — but the `no-shorefade` arm at native k answers the question that matters for the MIN BAR. Western Rootlands: no-shorefade width **1** (pinned, all three thresholds), fixed width **15**. So the waterline widening is carried ENTIRELY by the shoreline ALPHA half, and the depth-COLOUR half contributes nothing to it. Both are still real; they do different jobs.
job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.what_i_falsified: **`gradient_width_px` IS NOT MONOTONIC IN k, and the build's headline says it is.** In the Deep Marshes width rises as k falls (5/7/13/19 for 4.5/2.6/1.4/0.35). In the Western Rootlands it does NOT: k 0.35 → **1**, k 1.4 → 13, k 1.9 → 15, k 2.6 → 14–15. The fade needs PARTIAL opacity to have a gradient; at k = 0.35 the water is transparent everywhere and the span collapses (7.854 against 12.6–15.4 on every other arm), so there is no transition left to measure. The Deep Marshes series was a segment of a curve, not a law, and 'monotonic and large' should not be quoted forward as a property of the mechanism.
job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.what_replicates: **LUMA'S k ORDERING REPLICATES IN A SECOND REGION, A SECOND SCENE AND A SECOND MASK.** Western Rootlands: k 0.35 → 103.648, k 1.4 → 105.933, k 1.9 → 106.607, k 2.6 → 107.278. Monotonic increasing in k, against a 0.009% drift floor. Deep Marshes: 57.608 / 65.853 / 68.053 / 69.066 for 0.35 / 1.4 / 2.6 / 4.5. Same direction, same shape, two regions.
job_1_the_strongest_result_attacked.the_region_k_reaching_the_gpu_verified_b: `gpu_state_before` in three of my OWN runs, walking the live scene: `water:deep-marshes` k = 4.5, `water:eastern-rootlands` 3.2, `water:western-rootlands` 1.9, `water:stone-wastes` 1.4, and one mesh named plain `water` still on the documented 2.0 fallback. Four distinct declared k values reached four distinct materials. `RI-WLD10` §8's per-region water model reaches a fragment shader for the first time in this project, and that claim is a measurement off the live materials, not an assertion.

job_2_delivered_or_invisible_the_verdict.the_question: Is this a MIN BAR component genuinely delivered, or a correct mechanism that is invisible where the game is played? The brief says both readings are defensible and the verdict must choose one and say why.
job_2_delivered_or_invisible_the_verdict.ruling: **GENUINELY DELIVERED. THE INVISIBILITY IS A PROPERTY OF THE REGION THREE ROUNDS CHOSE TO STAND IN, NOT OF THE BUILD — AND I CAN SAY THAT ONLY BECAUSE I PHOTOGRAPHED A SECOND REGION, WHICH IS THE EXPERIMENT THE BUILD NAMED AND COULD NOT AFFORD.**
why: THE COLOUR HALF IS NOT INERT — IT IS INERT AT k = 4.5. The build's most self-damaging number is the `no-shorefade` arm reading 70.418 against the r2 arm's 70.428 in the Deep Marshes: 0.014%, inside its own 0.013% drift floor. I reproduced that reading's SHAPE in the Western Rootlands and it inverts: `no-shorefade` **112.622** against prefix **113.701**, a fall of 1.079 luma — **~120× the 0.009% drift floor at that pose**, and about 68× the Deep Marshes effect. The depth-based colour works. It does nothing at k = 4.5 because 4.5 means 0.67 m of visibility, which is what `RI-WLD10` §8 says the Deep Marshes IS.

THE FADE IS NOT 1 px — IT IS 1 px WHERE THERE IS NO WATERLINE. The build reports width 1 on both arms at all four eye-level bearings and at the vista, and treats that as the honest limit of its delivery. In the Western Rootlands, at top-down, the same code reads prefix **1** → fixed **15**, pinned mask, three thresholds, control 15. The r2 verdict's own proposed acceptance for remedy (b) asked for 'a new gradient-width measure showing the transition takes >= 15 px'. That number is hit.

THE DEEP MARSHES CONTAINS NO SHORELINE AT ALL, AND I CHECKED THIS BY EYE RATHER THAN BY ARITHMETIC. `RI-WLD10` §8 gives it WCI **0.86**, class 'drowned', signature 'black standing water with no tide and no bottom you want to find'. The top-down water mask is 87.9% of the frame; the water-hidden frame at the same pose shows vegetation clumps and fallen logs scattered across open marsh and NO land mass. So `distanceFromLand` at the pose that produced the build's whole k series is measuring distance from REED CLUMPS, not from a bank — which is a legitimate depth probe (clumps sit on shallow bed) but is NOT `RI-VIS04` §9's TELL, which is about where the water plane intersects the terrain.

AND THE ONE FRAME THE BUILD SAID HAD A BANK DOES NOT. The status file retracts two of its three close-ups and keeps the third: 'shore-close-c is the only one of the three with a real bank in it.' I opened both arms of `shore-close-c`. There is no bank in it. It is open marsh with reed clumps and trunks to the horizon, the two arms are indistinguishable, and its ShoreDelta of 0.033 — the only pose in the round to clear 0.03 — is measuring water-near-reeds against water-away-from-reeds. **All three close-ups are shoreless, and the build's partial retraction was itself too generous.** Four agents have now named this shot; I took it, in a region that has one.
job_2_delivered_or_invisible_the_verdict.the_consequence_that_belongs_to_the_orch: F7 has spent three rounds, three builders and three critics measuring a shoreline feature in the province's most drowned region. That is not a build defect and no build could have fixed it from inside its own brief. It is now written into `RI-VIS03` M12a §4 so the next round cannot repeat it.

job_3_the_bar_finding_that_unmakes_a_fai.the_question: Clause (b) may be decided by choice of bearing rather than by any shader. If so, r2's clause-(b) failure was an artefact and `RI-VIS03` M12 needs a declared bearing set.
job_3_the_bar_finding_that_unmakes_a_fai.ruling: **CONFIRMED, AND WORSE THAN THE BUILD REPORTED. r2's CLAUSE-(b) FAILURE AT 0.004 SHORT DOES NOT STAND AS A JUDGEMENT OF THE SHADER.**
job_3_the_bar_finding_that_unmakes_a_fai.the_measurement_re_derived_by_me_from_th: On ONE unchanged arm — the round-2 shader — `FresnelDelta` across the seven Deep Marshes poses reads 0.00629 / 0.02666 / 0.05316 / 0.09465 / 0.11613 / 0.12057 / 0.12817. Min 0.00629, max 0.12817, spread **0.12188**, ratio **20.4×**. **Five of seven poses clear the `>= 0.05` band on the arm that was failed at 0.04599.** In the Western Rootlands the same arm reads −0.08972 / −0.01399 / +0.07982 / +0.09637 / +0.13020 / +0.15514 — a range of **0.245 that spans the sign**, on a shader that did not change between readings.
job_3_the_bar_finding_that_unmakes_a_fai.so: A band that one shader both comfortably passes and comfortably fails, by pose alone, was not gating the build. The r2 verdict's clause-(b) FAIL is correct as arithmetic at the pose it chose and is not evidence about the water. I am recording that against a ruling my own brief says the orchestrator endorsed.
job_3_the_bar_finding_that_unmakes_a_fai.what_i_did_about_it_CRITIC_DOCTRINE_1_3: Extended the bar in the same pass. `RI-VIS03` §M12 gains **M12a — the declared pose set**: ≥ 4 poses ≥ 90° apart, declared before measuring, every pose on its own line, **no mean over poses**, **a band is met only at the WORST pose**, at least one `water_edge` pose with a real water/land boundary, and a WCI rule naming when a region cannot supply one. Plus the pinned-mask requirement below. `provenance: constructed`, marked ADD-only, and marked explicitly as something that may cause a FAIL and may never cause a PASS. `node tools/roadmap-coverage.mjs` — all gates green after the edit.
job_3_the_bar_finding_that_unmakes_a_fai.and_it_is_bounded: It removes a degree of freedom and relaxes no threshold. **It is not the reason for any score in this verdict**: every item here is failed on rows that predate it. Its only effect on this round is that it forbids me quoting the 0.128 close-pose readings as a pass, which I do not.

the_mask_is_part_of_the_instrument_and_i.what: **THE SINGLE MOST REUSABLE THING I FOUND, AND IT IS A DEFECT IN THE WHOLE F7 INSTRUMENT FAMILY ACROSS ALL THREE ROUNDS.** `WATER_MASK` is derived per-arm by differencing the arm's frame against a water-hidden frame at |dRGB| > 6. An arm that changes the water's ALPHA changes which pixels clear that threshold, so the two arms of a comparison are then scored over DIFFERENT PIXEL SETS. Rounds 1 and 2 touched only the reflection weight, so it never bit. Round 3 touches alpha, so it bites now.
the_mask_is_part_of_the_instrument_and_i.measured_not_argued: Western Rootlands, `eye-yaw000`, both arms. Per-arm masks: prefix 319,286 px, fixed 337,370 px — the fixed arm's mask grew **5.7%**. Per-arm `FresnelDelta`: **+0.14827 → −0.14524**, a sign flip and a −0.293 catastrophe. **Recomputed over ONE pinned mask (the prefix arm's): +0.14827 → +0.16112** — a small gain. `ShoreDelta` per-arm: 0.02418 → **0.09268**, which would have been a 3.8× rise clearing the `>= 0.03` band for the first time. Pinned: 0.02418 → 0.02144, a small fall, still failing.
the_mask_is_part_of_the_instrument_and_i.so: The per-arm mask manufactured BOTH a catastrophic false regression and a spurious pass, at the same pose, in the same pair of frames. It cuts both ways and it must be pinned. Where round 3's improvement survives pinning it is smaller but real: at `d-water-edge` per-arm FresnelDelta −0.08972 → −0.01412 becomes −0.08972 → −0.02383 pinned; `ShoreDelta` 0.03364 → 0.01023 becomes 0.03364 → 0.01466.
the_mask_is_part_of_the_instrument_and_i.written_into_the_corpus: Yes — `RI-VIS03` M12a's closing paragraph. Belongs in HAZARDS too, alongside the ordinal/phase confound; I did not write that entry and say so below.

normal_energy_has_been_measurable_for_tw.what: **M12 `NormalEnergy` IS MEASURED, IT PASSES ITS BAND, AND THE ROUND REPORTED IT AS UNMEASURED.** The r3 status file says: 'NormalEnergy and ReflCorr report unmeasurable at every one of the nine poses I took, with the same two reasons all three prior rounds recorded.' Its OWN artifact — `artifacts/W1-F7-WATER-r3/look/sweep.json` — carries `NormalEnergy` with a number and `normalReason: null` at **all seven look poses on both arms**, i.e. 14 of 14 rows.
normal_energy_has_been_measurable_for_tw.the_values: 0.07584, 0.13303, 0.13528, 0.14606, 0.15964, 0.16737, 0.16776, 0.16862, 0.17540, 0.19294, 0.22481, 0.22573, 0.27919, 0.27987, 0.30342, 0.30422, 0.33965, 0.34201 across the build's look run and my Western Rootlands runs. `RI-VIS03` M12's band is `>= 0.035`, fail `< 0.012`. **Every reading passes, by 2× to 10×.** Re-derived by me independently with `tools/metrics/lib/vis03.mjs` against the frames on disk before I looked at the build's JSON.
normal_energy_has_been_measurable_for_tw.why_it_was_missed: `NormalEnergy` needs a 128×128 square lying entirely inside the water mask. At `topdown-120` and the deck vista the mask is large but ragged — reed clumps everywhere — so it returns null, and those are the only two poses rounds 1 and 2 measured. The seven close/eye poses round 3 added are the first poses in this piece's history where the metric CAN run, and the round shipped an inherited 'unmeasurable' over its own output. This is CLAUDE.md §0b's exact shape arriving from the inside: an assertion carried from a sibling's summary rather than read from the artifact in front of it.
normal_energy_has_been_measurable_for_tw.the_caveat_i_will_not_omit: `NormalEnergy` is HFR — high-frequency energy over a water window. The build itself recorded, unprompted, that every close frame carries **heavy dither stipple across the water**, and I confirm it by eye in five frame pairs on BOTH arms. Dither stipple is high-frequency energy. So a passing `NormalEnergy` may be scoring an alpha-dither artefact as ripple detail, which is S52's shape again. I score it PASS because the corpus's own instrument, run per its own definition, passes it — and I name the confound and the test that would separate it (`RI-VIS04` §8's supersample test: recapture at 2× and downsample; genuine ripple survives, aliased stipple collapses). Nobody has run it.

instrument_findings.the_phase_freeze_did_what_the_build_says: CONFIRMED from the build's own band run, re-read by me: three replicates of the untouched arm at three ordinals read mean_luma 72.526 / 72.527 / 72.548 (range **0.022**) and `gradient_width_px` 1 / 1 / 1 (range **0**), against the r2 critic's 5-replicate vista band of 2.069 on luma. `FresnelDelta` did NOT collapse — 0.00664 / 0.01496 / 0.01851, range **0.01187**, slightly WIDER than the r2 critic's 0.00943. The build's reading is right and it corrects the r2 critic's account: freezing `uWaterPhase` fixes the water and not the scene, `stepFrames` still advances the canopy and the reflection target between captures, and both of the quantities that read the reflected canopy still move. Phase was never FresnelDelta's problem.
instrument_findings.the_width_measure_has_a_band_and_the_bui: `gradient_width_px` is integer-valued and its `d10` is pinned at 2 in **every one of the 16 top-down rows** the build published, so the measure is really `d90 − 2` — a one-sided plateau-onset estimate. Its published range of 0 comes from the deck vista, where it is 1 on every arm and therefore degenerate. At the poses that carry the result there is no replicate band: my own control-vs-fixed pairs read 15 vs 15 (thr 6) and 16 vs 15 (thr 4) in the Western Rootlands and 5 vs 5 in the Deep Marshes, so the band is about **±2 at n = 2**. The 1-vs-15 contrast is ~7× that; the build's 4-vs-5-vs-3 contrast in the Deep Marshes is INSIDE it and should not have been quoted as separating the null.
instrument_findings.the_null_is_only_a_null_at_the_k_it_was_: `nullTrans` is a fixed constant. At k = 4.5 the value 0.08 happens to sit near the real mean transmittance, so the null matched luminance and the comparison was fair. At k = 1.9 the same 0.08 reproduces only 11% of the luma fall (112.935 against fixed 106.607 from prefix 113.701) — which looks like the null failing and is actually the null being mis-calibrated. I re-ran it at 0.74 to match, and report the matched row rather than the flattering one.

a_depth_based_colour.remedy_as_written: Bind the scene depth texture, reconstruct water column depth per fragment, and drive the body colour by Beer-Lambert against the region's declared `k`. Acceptance: two regions whose `water.json` k differs by >= 2.0 must differ in measured water-body colour by a stated margin at the same pose and tide; and the Deep Marshes' rendered colour must be consistent with k = 4.5.
a_depth_based_colour.mechanism: NOT AS SPECIFIED. No scene depth texture is bound; the column depth comes from province.js's per-vertex colour. `grep -c 'depthTexture\|tDepth\|depthFade' game/src/render/water.js` returns **0**, run by me this turn, and the builder deliberately kept those identifiers out of its comments so the detector could not be satisfied by prose. That is the honest way to fail a detector and I credit it.
a_depth_based_colour.outcome: **DELIVERED AND MEASURED.** The body colour is `mix(esDeepCol, esBedCol, exp(-max(uWaterK,.05)*esPath))` with `esPath = esDepthM*(1 + 1/max(esView,.22))`, i.e. down through the column and back out along the view ray. Four distinct declared k values reach four distinct materials, verified off the live scene in three of my own runs. Mean water luma is monotonic in k in TWO regions.
a_depth_based_colour.acceptance_clause_scored: **PARTIAL, AND CLOSER THAN ANY ROUND HAS BEEN.** 'Two regions whose k differs by >= 2.0': I photographed the Deep Marshes (4.5) and the Western Rootlands (1.9), Δk = 2.6. They differ enormously in measured water-body colour — but at DIFFERENT poses in different scenes, so the clause's 'at the same pose and tide' is not satisfiable across regions and never was. What IS unconfounded is the k-substitution series within each region: Δk 2.6 → Δluma 1.446 in the Western Rootlands (161× the drift floor) and Δluma 1.013 in the Deep Marshes (113× its floor). 'The Deep Marshes' rendered colour is consistent with k = 4.5': **NOT ESTABLISHED, and the build says so.** There is no reference photometry for 0.67 m visibility water in this repo and nobody invented one.
a_depth_based_colour.score: PASS on presence and on k-consumption. FAIL on the absolute-colour half, unevidenced, 0 fail-closed.

b_shoreline_depth_fade.remedy_as_written: With the depth read available, fade colour and alpha over the depth difference. Acceptance PAIRED per S59: `ShoreDelta` back >= 0.03 AND a new gradient-width measure showing the transition takes >= 15 px at the deck vista.
b_shoreline_depth_fade.outcome: **HALF THE PAIRED ACCEPTANCE IS MET AND HALF IS NOT — WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT PAIRING IS FOR.**

why_i_confirm_rather_than_merely_defer: The previous shader's only depth signal was wired with the WRONG SIGN — `diffuseColor` carries province.js's q, which rises with depth, and it entered the body colour as `+diffuseColor.rgb*.21`, so deeper water came out brighter. I verified the inversion is now correct: province.js:1559 writes `q = .43+.57*clamp(depth/1.35,0,1)` into all three vertex-colour channels as (q, .96q, .88q); the vendored three's `color_vertex` chunk is a bare `vColor *= color` with no gamma decode, so `vColor.r` IS q; the shader divides it back out with `esAlbedo = diffuseColor.rgb/max(esQ,.43)`, which is correct for all three channels because all three scale linearly in q; and the regional water materials carry `vertexColors: true` (province.js:413) while `mats.farWater` does not, which is exactly the `#ifdef USE_COLOR` fallback the shader documents. Removing an inverted depth term is right even if every clause scored 0.

The preservation property is algebra and it holds: at q = 1 the new expression reduces to the old one exactly, and at k = 4.5 `esTrans = exp(-4.5*2.7) ≈ 5e-6`, so the change cannot act above 1.35 m of column in the Deep Marshes. The measurements agree — no eye-level FresnelDelta pair moves by more than the instrument's own band.
